newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bank shares seen continuing up all year.
newsitem.headline: Danish bank shares seen continuing up all year.

text.p: Analysts predicted on Friday that Danish bank shares would continue their upward trend for the rest of the year following major rises in the first six months of 1997.

"We are seeing a lot of positive forecasts about Danish banks at the moment, but even if we maybe experience a period of correction in the coming weeks, it will not be dramatic and bank paper will continue upwards again," one analyst told Reuters.
Danish bank shares have surged ahead this year, with shares in Den Danske Bank, Denmark's biggest bank, almost 60 percent up so far and rival Unidanmark and BG Bank up around 40 percent.
The banking sector share index on the Copenhagen bourse has climbed 45 percent this year, compared to a total share index rise of 30 percent.
In the past week alone, Danske Bank and Unidanmark stock has risen 10 percent in value, with BG Bank up 2.5 percent.

Another analyst, who also requested anonymity, pointed to a 'buy' recommendation for Den Danske and Unidanmark to be issued next Monday by Britain's SBC Warburg, along with a forecast that Unidanmark shares would rise to 520 crowns during the year ahead.
At 1100 GMT on Friday Unidanmark was 13 crowns higher at 443 crowns, with Den Danske and BG Bank up eight and 13 crowns respectively at 750 and 403 crowns.
The possibility of mergers in the Danish bank industry has also fuelled interest in bank shares.
Rumours have circulated on markets in recent weeks of a possible new strategic alliance or merger between BG Bank and the second biggest bank Unidanmark, despite denials by BG Bank.

"I can understand that some analysts consider a merger between BG Bank and Unidanmark to be obvious because of the possibility of making considerable costs savings, but we have not discussed the matter, nor do we have any plans to do so," BG Bank managing director Henrik Thufason told Reuters this week.
